description: A pure CALCULATION node — fold a matrix down to fewer numbers: Sum, Min, Max, Mean or Product, over the whole matrix, per row, or per column. Draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: a matrix in, a smaller matrix out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

WHY IT EXISTS: every other matrix node is shape-preserving or shape-combining — none of them can answer "what is the total / the smallest / the average". Reduce is the aggregate step, and its 1×1 result BROADCASTS back over any shape through Matrix Operations, so a whole-matrix statistic can be applied per row.

AXIS:
• All → one number (1×1). Total area, first event time, global min.
• Per row → N×1, folding each row across its columns.
• Per column → 1×C, folding each column down its rows. Column sums of an N×2 point list give (Σx, Σy) — divide by N for the centroid.

TWO IDIOMS worth knowing:
• SIGNED AREA / WINDING — Vector Product (Cross) of a point list against Shift Rows(-1) gives the per-edge shoelace terms; Reduce (Sum, All) totals them. The result is 2×area, and its SIGN is the polygon's winding (positive = counter-clockwise). Divide it by its own absolute value to get ±1, then multiply your normals by that to make them face inward whatever the winding.
• SMALLEST POSITIVE — Reduce (Min) counts negatives and zeros too. To get the smallest POSITIVE entry, take 1/x first (Matrix Operations Divide, with A = [[1]]), Reduce (Max), then invert again: non-positive entries become ≤ 0 and lose automatically.

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
